correctness.rationale: Disjoint column supports make the modulus diagonal, with the v-entry r_v=||Te_v||. For r_v>0 the polar update gives edge weight lambda_vu(r_u/r_v)^t, and gives a zero outgoing column if r_v=0. The resulting p-mass at v is at most b_v^(1-t)(sum_children b_u)^t, by bounding each r_u in the weighted quadratic mean by (sum_children b_u)^(1/p). This remains valid for countably many children, vanishing weights, and p<1. Scalar weighted AM–GM then bounds it by ((1-t)I+tQ)b, where Q adds child masses. Unique parents make Q positive and contractive on l1; Q^k counts each vertex once exactly when it has depth at least k. Iteration and the binomial expansion thus give the precise depth-weighted sum over the original masses, including n=0, and justify that every iterate is in the same Schatten class. Since each vertex has finite depth, dominated convergence gives the endpoint result. Splitting at K, and setting K=floor(nt/2)+1 for the Chernoff estimate, gives precisely the claimed strict depth tail and e^(-nt/8). On L equally weighted positive path edges of normalized weight L^(-1/p), exactly one more terminal edge vanishes in each iteration up to L, so the p-energy is (L-n)/L for n<L and gives the stated supremum by sending L to infinity.
residual_risks: No conclusion for rootless shifts or arbitrary compact operators, and no assertion about t=1. No fresh numerical run or formal certification is claimed.

evidence: Stanković's general Schatten theorem starts in S_q with q<p, with Remark 5.7 distinguishing the unresolved general diagonal endpoint. Proposition 5.8 already treats every p>0 on a unilateral path; Corollary 5.9 also treats direct sums with finite-dimensional operators. Bala's general compact result uses operator norm for the ordinary transform, not the same Schatten quasi-norm.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A genuine branching example evades both Stanković extensions: assign two nonzero root edges and distinct decaying outgoing weights on the two infinite rays with p-masses comparable to 1/(k log^2 k). It is in S_p and in no S_q for q<p. It is injective and quasinilpotent, hence has no nonzero finite-dimensional reducing summand; W*W and WW* do not commute because of the unequal child norms and the common root. Thus it is also not an orthogonal sum of unilateral shifts.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Turning the known nonlinear polar update into a scalar positive mass comparison that survives both arbitrary branching and p<1, then evaluating the exact loss of mass due to the root, is the additional argument. In particular, one cannot infer convergence in S_p from operator-norm decay and mere boundedness in S_p.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A version of the claim in column-mass language is domination by the killed ancestor transition ((1-t)I+tQ)^n, summed over all vertices, with a different survival probability at each depth. A scalar geometric product along a single path neither states this column inequality at a split nor constrains its incoming branch masses.

value.rationale: Equal-ideal convergence at every p>0 is a meaningful endpoint question, including the quasi-Banach regime. This solves it for a natural nontrivial branching class with operators outside the previous smaller-ideal and direct-sum hypotheses, and provides usable quantitative decay governed by initial depth tails. The simple path witness clarifies why a unit-normalized, depth-free uniform rate is not an acceptable replacement.
residual_risks: The estimate is not asserted to be pointwise sharp on every tree and does not settle the general compact Schatten endpoint.
